content.overview: BNS s. 335 — Making a false document.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Making a false document. BNS restatement of IPC 464. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 464. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 335 is the rule on “Making a false document”. The section provides that . A person is said to make a false document or false electronic record—. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 335 exists so that “Making a false document” has a closed legal test in Chapter XVIII — Of Offences Relating to Documents and to Property Marks. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: False documents, forgery, using a forged electronic record, property marks.

The provision in detail
335.. A person is said to make a false document or false electronic record—

(A) Who dishonestly or fraudulently—

(i) makes, signs, seals or executes a document or part of a document;

(ii) makes or transmits any electronic record or part of any electronic record;

(iii) affixes any electronic signature on any electronic record;

(iv) makes any mark denoting the execution of a document or the authenticity of the electronic signature,

with the intention of causing it to be believed that such document or part of document, electronic record or electronic signature was made, signed, sealed, executed, transmitted or affixed by or by the authority of a person by whom or by whose authority he knows that it was not made, signed, sealed, executed or affixed; or

(B) Who without lawful authority, dishonestly or fraudulently, by cancellation or otherwise, alters a document or an electronic record in any material part thereof, after it has been made, executed or affixed with electronic signature either by himself or by any other person, whether such person be living or dead at the time of such alteration; or

(C) Who dishonestly or fraudulently causes any person to sign, seal, execute or alter a document or an electronic record or to affix his electronic signature on any electronic record knowing that such person by reason of unsoundness of mind or intoxication cannot, or that by reason of deception practised upon him, he does not know the contents of the document or electronic record or the nature of the alteration

Essential ingredients
1. . A person is said to make a false document or false electronic record—
2. (A) Who dishonestly or fraudulently—
3. (i) makes, signs, seals or executes a document or part of a document;
4. (ii) makes or transmits any electronic record or part of any electronic record;
5. (iii) affixes any electronic signature on any electronic record;
6. (iv) makes any mark denoting the execution of a document or the authenticity of the electronic signature,
7. with the intention of causing it to be believed that such document or part of document, electronic record or electronic signature was made, signed, sealed, executed, transmitted or affixed by or by the authority of a person by whom or by whose authority he knows that it was not made, signed, sealed, executed or affixed; or
8. (B) Who without lawful authority, dishonestly or fraudulently, by cancellation or otherwise, alters a document or an electronic record in any material part thereof, after it has been made, executed or affixed with electronic signature either by himself or by any other person, whether such person be living or dead at the time of such alteration; or
9. (C) Who dishonestly or fraudulently causes any person to sign, seal, execute or alter a document or an electronic record or to affix his electronic signature on any electronic record knowing that such person by reason of unsoundness of mind or intoxication cannot, or that by reason of deception practised upon him, he does not know the contents of the document or electronic record or the nature of the alteration

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). A has a letter of credit upon B for rupees 10,000, written by Z. A, in order to defraud B, adds cipher to the 10,000, and makes the sum 1,00,000 intending that it may be believed by B that Z so wrote the letter. A has committed forgery

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 335 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (b). A, without Z’s authority, affixes Z’s seal to a document purporting to be a conveyance of an estate from Z to A, with the intention of selling the estate to B and thereby of obtaining from B the purchase-money. A has committed forgery

Exam use: quote illustration (b), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 335 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (c). A picks up a cheque on a banker signed by B, payable to bearer, but without any sum having been inserted in the cheque. A fraudulently fills up the cheque by inserting the sum of ten thousand rupees. A commits forgery

Exam use: quote illustration (c), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 335 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (d). A leaves with B, his agent, a cheque on a banker, signed by A, without inserting the sum payable and authorises B to fill up the cheque by inserting a sum not exceeding ten thousand rupees for the purpose of making certain payments. B fraudulently fills up the cheque by inserting the sum of twenty thousand rupees. B commits forgery

Exam use: quote illustration (d), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 335 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (e). A draws a bill of exchange on himself in the name of B without B’s authority, intending to discount it as a genuine bill with a banker and intending to take up the bill on its maturity. Here, as A draws the bill with intent to deceive the banker by leading him to suppose that he had the security of B, and thereby to discount the bill, A is guilty of forgery

Exam use: quote illustration (e), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 335 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (f). Z’s will contains these words—“I direct that all my remaining property be equally divided between A, B and C”. A dishonestly scratches out B’s name, intending that it may be believed that the whole was left to himself and C. A has committed forgery

Exam use: quote illustration (f), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 335 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (g). A endorses a Government promissory note and makes it payable to Z or his order by writing on the bill the words “Pay to Z or his order” and signing the endorsement. B dishonestly erases the words “Pay to Z or his order”, and thereby converts the special endorsement into a blank endorsement. B commits forgery

Exam use: quote illustration (g), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 335 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (h). A sells and conveys an estate to Z. A afterwards, in order to defraud Z of his estate, executes a conveyance of the same estate to B, dated six months earlier than the date of the conveyance to Z, intending it to be believed that he had conveyed the estate to B before he conveyed it to Z. A has committed forgery

Exam use: quote illustration (h), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 335 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (i). Z dictates his will to A. A intentionally writes down a different legatee from the legatee named by Z, and by representing to Z that he has prepared the will according to his instructions, induces Z to sign the will. A has committed forgery

Exam use: quote illustration (i), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 335 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (j). A writes a letter and signs it with B’s name without B’s authority, certifying that A is a man of good character and in distressed circumstances from unforeseen misfortune, intending by means of such letter to obtain alms from Z and other persons. Here, as A made a false document in order to induce Z to part with property, A has committed forgery

Exam use: quote illustration (j), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 335 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (k). A without B’s authority writes a letter and signs it in B’s name certifying to A’s character, intending thereby to obtain employment under Z. A has committed forgery in as much as he intended to deceive Z by the forged certificate, and thereby to induce Z to enter into an express or implied contract for service

Exam use: quote illustration (k), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 335 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (l). A signs his own name to a bill of exchange, intending that it may be believed that the bill was drawn by another person of the same name. A has committed forgery

Exam use: quote illustration (l), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 335 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (m). A writes the word “accepted” on a piece of paper and signs it with Z’s name, in order that B may afterwards write on the paper a bill of exchange drawn by B upon Z, and negotiate the bill as though it had been accepted by Z. A is guilty of forgery; and if B, knowing the fact, draws the bill upon the paper pursuant to A’s intention, B is also guilty of forgery

Exam use: quote illustration (m), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 335 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (n). A picks up a bill of exchange payable to the order of a different person of the same name. A endorses the bill in his own name, intending to cause it to be believed that it was endorsed by the person to whose order it was payable; here A has committed forgery

Exam use: quote illustration (n), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 335 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (o). A purchases an estate sold under execution of a decree against B. B, after the seizure of the estate, in collusion with Z, executes a lease of the estate, to Z at a nominal rent and for a long period and dates the lease six months prior to the seizure, with intent to defraud A, and to cause it to be believed that the lease was granted before the seizure. B, though he executes the lease in his own name, commits forgery by antedating it

Exam use: quote illustration (o), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 335 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (p). A, a trader, in anticipation of insolvency, lodges effects with B for A’s benefit, and with intent to defraud his creditors; and in order to give a colour to the transaction, writes a promissory note binding himself to pay to B a sum for value received, and antedates the note, intending that it may be believed to have been made before A was on the point of insolvency. A has committed forgery under the first head of the definition

Exam use: quote illustration (p), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 335 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (q). A draws a bill of exchange upon a fictitious person, and fraudulently accepts the bill in the name of such fictitious person with intent to negotiate it. A commits forgery

Exam use: quote illustration (q), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 335 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Explanations
Explanation 1.—A man’s signature of his own name may amount to forgery

Explanation 2.—The making of a false document in the name of a fictitious person, intending it to be believed that the document was made by a real person, or in the name of a deceased person, intending it to be believed that the document was made by the person in his lifetime, may amount to forgery

Explanation 3.—For the purposes of this section, the expression “affixing electronic signature” shall have the meaning assigned to it in clause (d) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Information Technology Act, 2000

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 335 (Making a false document) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 335 (Making a false document), Chapter XVIII — Of Offences Relating to Documents and to Property Marks.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) . A person is said to make a false document or false electronic record—
   (2) (A) Who dishonestly or fraudulently—
   (3) (i) makes, signs, seals or executes a document or part of a document;
   (4) (ii) makes or transmits any electronic record or part of any electronic record;
   (5) (iii) affixes any electronic signature on any electronic record;
   (6) (iv) makes any mark denoting the execution of a document or the authenticity of the electronic signature,
   (7) with the intention of causing it to be believed that such document or part of document, electronic record or electronic signature was made, signed, sealed, executed, transmitted or affixed by or by the authority of a person by whom or by whose authority he knows that it was not made, signed, sealed, executed or affixed; or
   (8) (B) Who without lawful authority, dishonestly or fraudulently, by cancellation or otherwise, alters a document or an electronic record in any material part thereof, after it has been made, executed or affixed with electronic signature either by himself or by any other person, whether such person be living or dead at the time of such alteration; or
Step 3 — Read every Explanation. An explanation is part of the section. Omitting it leaves the analysis incomplete and vulnerable to rebuttal.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 335 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

Classification and Sentencing: Structured under Chapter XVIII penal tiers.

essentialIngredients: . A person is said to make a false document or false electronic record—
(i) makes, signs, seals or executes a document or part of a document
(ii) makes or transmits any electronic record or part of any electronic record
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 335 defines making a false document or electronic record (former IPC 464). A person makes a false document if they: (1) dishonestly or fraudulently make, sign, seal, or execute a document/record, or make any mark denoting execution, with the intention of causing it to be believed that it was made by authority of someone who did not authorize it; (2) dishonestly or fraudulently cancel or alter a material part without lawful authority; or (3) dishonestly cause any person of unsound mind or under deception to sign or execute.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of making a false document under Section 335 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 335.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 335 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Making a false document (s. 335) vs Forgery (s. 336): Section 335 defines the mechanical fabrication; Section 336 defines the offence of forgery when a false document is made with specific fraudulent intent.

False document vs False statement: A false document is a document that tells a lie about its own origin or authorship; a document containing untrue statements is not a false document if genuinely signed by the author.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 335 for conduct relating to making a false document.
Rule: Under BNS s. 335, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 335.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 335 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
